questions.question_text: A company wants to introduce a new genetically modified crop for cultivation in India. According to NCERT, which organisation set up by the Indian Government makes decisions regarding the validity of GM research and the safety of introducing GM organisms for public services?

options.text: The US Patent and Trademark Office

solution.concept: Regulation of GM organisms in India
solution.explanation: NCERT: the Indian Government has set up organisations such as GEAC, which will make decisions regarding the validity of GM research and the safety of introducing GM-organisms for public services. (NCERT expands GEAC as the Genetic Engineering Approval Committee; the committee is now officially called the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee, which is why the option gives only the abbreviation.)
steps: GM organism for public use -> safety and validity decided by GEAC
solution.why_others_wrong: NACO works on AIDS awareness, CDRI developed the pill Saheli, and the US Patent and Trademark Office granted the Basmati patent; none decides on GM organisms in India.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Ethical Issues
solution.final_answer: Option C: GEAC

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (gene or DNA introduced) with List-II (condition it was used to control).

List-I:
A. cryIAc and cryIIAb
B. cryIAb
C. Nematode-specific genes producing sense and anti-sense RNA
D. Functional ADA cDNA

List-II:
I. An immune disorder in a child, treated by gene therapy
II. Infection of tobacco roots by Meloidegyne incognitia
III. Damage by the corn borer
IV. Damage to cotton by bollworms

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the proteins encoded by cryIAc and cryIIAb control the cotton bollworms, and that of cryIAb controls the corn borer. Nematode-specific genes introduced into tobacco produced sense and anti-sense RNA, which protected the roots from Meloidegyne incognitia by RNAi. A functional ADA cDNA was introduced into the lymphocytes of a child with ADA deficiency (ADA is crucial for the immune system to function).
solution.why_others_wrong: The commonest slip swaps the cotton genes (cryIAc, cryIIAb) with the corn gene (cryIAb); the nematode genes act through RNAi, not as cry toxins.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about RNA interference (RNAi) are correct according to NCERT?

(a) RNAi takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence.
(b) The source of the complementary RNA could be an infection by viruses having RNA genomes.
(c) The source of the complementary RNA could also be mobile genetic elements (transposons) that replicate via an RNA intermediate.
(d) RNAi is a method of cellular defence found only in prokaryotes.
(e) RNAi works only when the Bt toxin protein is also present in the cell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: RNAi takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence. It involves silencing of a specific mRNA due to a complementary dsRNA molecule. The source of this complementary RNA could be from an infection by viruses having RNA genomes or mobile genetic elements (transposons) that replicate via an RNA intermediate. RNAi has nothing to do with the Bt toxin.
steps: (e) false - RNAi and Bt toxin are separate strategies
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) contradicts (a), since NCERT says RNAi occurs in all eukaryotes; (e) mixes up two unrelated pest-resistance methods.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

Match List-I (use of transgenic animals) with List-II (reason, as classified in NCERT).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the RNAi strategy against Meloidegyne incognitia, suppose that by mistake a gene essential to the tobacco plant itself, rather than a nematode-specific gene, is introduced so that it produces both sense and anti-sense RNA in the plant cells. What is the most likely result?

options.text: The nematode would still be killed, because any dsRNA is toxic to nematodes
Nothing would happen, because RNA interference does not occur in plants
The dsRNA formed would silence the matching mRNA of the tobacco plant, harming the plant rather than the nematode
The plant would become resistant to bollworms, because the dsRNA acts like the Bt toxin

solution.explanation: NCERT: RNAi involves silencing of a specific mRNA due to a complementary dsRNA molecule that binds to and prevents translation of the mRNA. In the tobacco example the dsRNA was made from nematode genes, so it silenced a specific mRNA of the nematode. RNAi occurs in all eukaryotes, so a dsRNA made from the plant's own gene would silence the matching mRNA of the plant itself.
steps: dsRNA silences the mRNA complementary to it
Plant gene used -> plant mRNA silenced -> plant harmed, nematode not targeted
solution.why_others_wrong: RNAi silences only the mRNA complementary to the dsRNA, so it is not a general nematode poison; RNAi occurs in all eukaryotes, plants included; and dsRNA does not act like the Bt toxin protein.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture
solution.final_answer: Option C: The dsRNA formed would silence the matching mRNA of the tobacco plant, harming the plant rather than the nematode

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Bt toxin genes are expressed in crop plants to make them resistant to insect pests.
Reason (R): After being activated by the alkaline pH of the insect gut, the Bt toxin binds to the midgut epithelial cells and creates pores that cause swelling and lysis of the cells, eventually killing the insect.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: Bt toxin genes isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis are incorporated into crop plants such as cotton, providing resistance to insects without the need for insecticides. The toxin kills the insect that eats the plant: the inactive protoxin is solubilised and activated by the alkaline gut pH, binds to the midgut epithelial cells and creates pores, causing swelling and lysis and eventually death. R explains why the expressing crop is resistant.
steps: R: true - the mode of action of Bt toxin
Insect eating the crop is killed -> crop protected -> R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: Both are NCERT statements, and the killing of feeding insects described in R is what gives the crop its resistance, so B, C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A foreign company uses neem, an Indian traditional herbal medicine, together with the traditional knowledge of the people, to make a commercial product and patents it, without authorisation from India or the people concerned and without any compensatory payment. Which of the following are correct according to NCERT?

(a) NCERT mentions neem among the Indian traditional herbal medicines on which attempts have been made to patent uses, products and processes.
(b) Use of bio-resources in this way, without proper authorisation and compensatory payment, is called biopiracy.
(c) The developing and the under-developed world is rich in biodiversity and traditional knowledge related to bio-resources.

Biopiracy is the term used to refer to the use of bio-resources by multinational companies and other organisations without proper authorisation from the countries and people concerned and without compensatory payment. Industrialised nations are rich financially but poor in biodiversity and traditional knowledge, whereas the developing and under-developed world is rich in them.
steps: (d) false - industrialised nations are poor in biodiversity
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) reverses which nations are rich in biodiversity, and (e) reverses the definition of biopiracy, so any option containing them is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Ethical Issues

Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Transgenic mice are being developed for use in testing the safety of the polio vaccine.
Reason (R): Over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the gene therapy given for ADA deficiency, lymphocytes from the patient's blood were grown in a culture outside the body.
Statement II: The functional ADA cDNA was introduced into these lymphocytes by biolistics (gene gun).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A tomato crop is badly damaged by beetles (coleopterans). Following NCERT's account of Bt crops, which transgenic approach would be most suitable?

options.text: Express cryIAc and cryIIAb, since these genes control every kind of insect
Introduce nematode-specific genes so that RNAi silences the beetles' mRNA
Express in tomato the toxin gene from a strain of Bacillus thuringiensis whose protein kills coleopterans
Introduce the genes used in golden rice, since vitamin A protects plants from beetles

solution.concept: Choosing Bt toxin genes for a target pest
solution.explanation: NCERT: some strains of Bacillus thuringiensis produce proteins that kill certain insects such as lepidopterans, coleopterans (beetles) and dipterans; most Bt toxins are insect-group specific, and the choice of genes depends upon the crop and the targeted pest. Bt toxin genes have been expressed in tomato among other crops. So the tomato should be given toxin genes from a strain whose protein kills coleopterans.
steps: Choose genes from a strain toxic to coleopterans and express them in tomato
solution.why_others_wrong: cryIAc and cryIIAb are named for cotton bollworms, and Bt toxins are not effective against every insect; RNAi with nematode genes would target a nematode, not beetles; golden rice genes improve nutrition, not pest resistance.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture
solution.final_answer: Option C: Express in tomato the toxin gene from a strain of Bacillus thuringiensis whose protein kills coleopterans

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Suppose that, instead of following Eli Lilly's approach, a company expressed in E. coli a single gene for human pro-insulin. Based on NCERT, what additional step would be needed to obtain functional insulin?

options.text: Addition of a C peptide, which mature insulin requires
Separation of chains A and B so that they are never joined
Conversion of the protein into DNA before injection
Removal of the C peptide, to convert the pro-hormone into mature insulin

solution.explanation: NCERT: in mammals, including humans, insulin is synthesised as a pro-hormone which contains an extra stretch called the C peptide; this C peptide is not present in mature insulin and is removed during maturation into insulin. The main challenge was getting insulin assembled into a mature form, which Eli Lilly avoided by making chains A and B separately and joining them by disulphide bonds. A pro-insulin product would still need its C peptide removed.
steps: Mature insulin lacks the C peptide
So the C peptide must be removed
solution.why_others_wrong: The C peptide is absent from mature insulin, so it must be removed, not added; chains A and B must be linked (by disulphide bridges) in functional insulin; and a protein is not converted into DNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Medicine (Genetically Engineered Insulin)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Removal of the C peptide, to convert the pro-hormone into mature insulin

Match List-I (problem) with List-II (solution described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Some patients developed allergy to insulin from slaughtered cattle and pigs
B. Genetically engineered lymphocytes are not immortal, so infusions must be repeated
C. Emphysema patients need human α-1-antitrypsin
D. People eating mainly rice may lack vitamin A

I. Golden rice

Which of the following statements correctly compare Bt cotton with the RNAi-based tobacco that resists Meloidegyne incognitia?

(a) In Bt cotton the protective molecule is a protein, whereas in the RNAi tobacco it is a double-stranded RNA.
(b) The genes used in Bt cotton come from a bacterium, whereas those used in the RNAi tobacco come from the pest (the nematode) itself.
(c) Vectors derived from Agrobacterium were used to introduce the nematode-specific genes into tobacco.
(d) Both strategies work by silencing a specific mRNA of the pest.
(e) Both strategies kill the pest by creating pores in the cells of its midgut.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: Bt cotton expresses cry genes isolated from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis; the toxin protein kills insects by binding to midgut epithelial cells and making pores. In the tobacco example, nematode-specific genes were introduced into the host plant using Agrobacterium vectors; they produced sense and anti-sense RNA, which formed dsRNA that silenced a specific mRNA of the nematode (RNAi).
steps: (b) true - bacterial genes vs nematode genes
(e) false - only the Bt toxin forms pores
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) applies only to RNAi and (e) only to the Bt toxin; each wrongly extends one mechanism to both crops.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only
